modules.title: Digital Literacy Basics
modules.description: Learn how to use smartphones, the internet, and basic apps to improve your life and work. This module introduces essential digital skills for communication, learning, and productivity.

lessons.title: Introduction to Smartphones
lessons.content: A smartphone is a mobile phone that has advanced features like internet access, a touchscreen, and the ability to install apps. It allows you to make calls, send messages, take photos, browse the web, and run mobile applications. Understanding your smartphone’s features helps you get the most out of it.
key_points: Smartphones are portable computers with touchscreen interfaces.
They run on operating systems like Android or iOS.
You can install apps for learning, business, health, and social interaction.
Most smartphones support mobile data, Wi-Fi, GPS, and cameras.
Popular brands include Samsung, Tecno, iPhone, Itel, and Infinix.
Learn how to turn your phone on/off, adjust volume, and manage battery.
lessons.local_example: Using WhatsApp on a Tecno phone to update customers on market prices.

lessons.title: Using the Internet
lessons.content: The internet connects people and information globally. It allows users to access websites, email, videos, and social media. Knowing how to navigate the internet safely and effectively opens opportunities for education, business, and social connection.
key_points: Use search engines like Google to find answers to questions.
Email helps in formal communication; apps like Gmail or Yahoo are common.
Social media platforms like Facebook, TikTok, and Instagram connect people and communities.
YouTube offers free learning videos on farming, cooking, tailoring, and more.
Always verify information and be careful of fake news or scams online.
Understand basic terms: website, browser, URL, link, download.
lessons.local_example: Searching for tailoring tutorials on YouTube and learning from them at home.

lessons.title: Mobile Apps for Everyday Use
lessons.content: Apps are small programs you install on smartphones to help with different tasks like chatting, learning, or running a business. Learning to download, install, and use apps helps you in many areas of daily life.
key_points: WhatsApp is used for messaging, voice notes, and group chats.
Facebook helps in marketing your small business and connecting with customers.
YouTube is a video platform where you can watch and upload content.
Zoom and Google Meet are used for online meetings or learning.
There are apps for budgeting, farming advice, health tips, and more.
Learn how to update apps and manage phone storage.
lessons.local_example: Using WhatsApp groups to advertise fresh mandasi in your community.

lessons.title: Creating and Managing Digital Accounts
lessons.content: Many online services require accounts. Knowing how to create, protect, and manage these accounts is essential for safe internet use.
key_points: Use strong, unique passwords for each account.
Avoid sharing passwords with others.
Keep recovery information (like phone number or email) up to date.
Log out from shared or public devices.
Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) when available for extra security.
lessons.local_example: Creating a Gmail account to send and receive job applications.

lessons.title: Staying Safe Online
lessons.content: Just like in real life, you need to protect yourself online. This involves keeping your information private and being careful about the websites and people you interact with.
key_points: Do not share passwords or personal details with strangers.
Avoid clicking suspicious links — they might be scams or viruses.
Use antivirus apps and keep your apps updated.
If a message or link looks too good to be true, it probably is.
Ask a trusted person for help if unsure about something online.
Recognize phishing attempts and scams.
lessons.local_example: Ignoring a fake message saying you've won a prize and reporting it to a teacher or parent.

lessons.title: Basic Troubleshooting and Maintenance
lessons.content: Learning how to solve common smartphone problems and maintain your device helps it last longer and perform better.
key_points: Restart your phone to fix minor issues.
Clear app cache to free up space and improve speed.
Delete unused apps to save storage.
Charge your phone with the correct charger to avoid damage.
Back up important data regularly, like photos and contacts.
lessons.local_example: Teaching elders in the community to back up photos of important events.

quiz.question: What is a smartphone?
options: A phone with apps and internet
quiz.answer: A phone with apps and internet

quiz.question: Why is the internet useful?
options: To find info, connect, and learn
quiz.answer: To find info, connect, and learn

quiz.question: Which app is good for chatting with family?
What should you avoid online?
What can you use YouTube for?
What is an example of safe internet use?

modules.title: Introd to Tailoring
modules.description: Learn the basics of measuring, cutting, sewing, and finishing clothes. This module helps you develop the skills needed to start tailoring at home or professionally, with step-by-step guidance from measurements to completed garments.

lessons.title: Taking Body Measurements
lessons.content: Measuring the body accurately is the first step to making clothes that fit well. Always use a soft tape measure and record the measurements clearly. Take multiple measurements if needed to ensure accuracy.
key_points: Measure key areas: chest, waist, hips, shoulder width, sleeve length, inseam, neck, and back length.
Ask the person to stand straight and relaxed while taking measurements.
Use the same unit of measurement consistently (inches or centimeters).
Record each measurement clearly to avoid mistakes during cutting.
Double-check measurements for accuracy before cutting fabric.
lessons.local_example: Measuring students in the village before sewing school uniforms for the new term.

lessons.title: Understanding Patterns and Fabric Layout
lessons.content: Patterns guide the cutting of fabric and help shape garments. Learning how to read and lay patterns on fabric saves material and ensures accuracy.
key_points: Use commercial or hand-drawn patterns as templates for cutting fabric.
Place patterns on fabric according to the grainline for better fit and drape.
Use weights or pins to hold patterns firmly on the fabric while cutting.
Learn to fold fabric correctly when working with double layers.
Plan fabric layout to minimize waste.
lessons.local_example: Using old newspaper to create basic pattern shapes before cutting chitenges.

lessons.title: Sewing Simple Clothes
lessons.content: Start sewing basic garments with hand stitching or a sewing machine. Practice simple projects to build confidence and skills.
key_points: Thread needles correctly for hand sewing or machine use.
Practice basic stitches: running stitch, backstitch, slip stitch, and hemming stitch.
Start with projects like pillowcases, shorts, aprons, or simple skirts.
Learn to sew straight seams and corners accurately.
Understand the importance of seam allowance in garment construction.
lessons.local_example: Sewing chitenges and aprons to sell at the local market.

lessons.title: Tools and Materials Needed
lessons.content: To begin tailoring, you need essential tools and materials that make the process easier and more professional.
key_points: Sewing machine or hand needles suitable for different fabrics.
Measuring tape, fabric scissors, pins, chalk or fabric marker.
Variety of fabrics such as cotton, polyester, and local prints.
Threads matching fabric colors, buttons, zippers, and elastic bands.
Iron and ironing board for pressing seams and finishing.
lessons.local_example: Using old clothes and recycled fabric to practice sewing at home.

lessons.title: Types of Fabrics and Their Uses
lessons.content: Different fabrics behave differently and are suitable for various types of clothing.
key_points: Cotton: breathable and easy to sew; ideal for everyday wear.
Polyester: durable and wrinkle-resistant; good for uniforms.
Silk: smooth and delicate; used for special occasion clothes.
Denim: strong and heavy; perfect for jeans and jackets.
Chitenge and other local fabrics: colorful and culturally significant.
lessons.local_example: Choosing the right fabric for school uniforms versus traditional wear.

lessons.title: Cutting Fabric Accurately
lessons.content: Cutting fabric correctly ensures the garment fits well and the fabric is not wasted.
key_points: Always cut on a flat surface with good lighting.
Use sharp fabric scissors, not regular scissors.
Follow the pattern edges closely without lifting the fabric.
Cut slowly and carefully, especially on curves and corners.
Keep fabric flat and avoid stretching while cutting.
lessons.local_example: Cutting fabric for a child's dress using a hand-drawn pattern.

lessons.title: Sewing Machine Basics and Maintenance
lessons.content: Knowing how to use and maintain a sewing machine will improve your sewing quality and machine lifespan.
key_points: Learn to thread the machine and wind the bobbin properly.
Adjust stitch length and tension according to fabric type.
Practice controlling machine speed for straight and even stitches.
Clean the machine regularly to remove lint and dust.
Oil moving parts as recommended to keep the machine running smoothly.
lessons.local_example: Maintaining an old sewing machine used in community tailoring workshops.

lessons.title: Finishing Techniques for Professional Results
lessons.content: Finishing touches make garments look neat and durable.
key_points: Press seams open or to one side with an iron for flat finishes.
Use hemming stitches to finish edges without fraying.
Add buttons, zippers, or hooks carefully and securely.
Use bias tape or binding to finish raw edges.
Check the garment fit and make adjustments if needed.
lessons.local_example: Adding buttons to a school uniform shirt to prepare it for sale.

lessons.title: Basic Clothing Alterations
lessons.content: Knowing simple alteration skills helps in fitting ready-made clothes or modifying garments.
key_points: Take in or let out seams to adjust size.
Shorten or lengthen hems and sleeves.
Replace broken buttons and repair torn seams.
Add darts to improve garment shape.
Use pins to mark adjustments before sewing.
lessons.local_example: Adjusting a secondhand dress to fit a smaller person.

lessons.title: Starting a Small Tailoring Business
lessons.content: Tailoring can be a profitable business with proper planning and customer care.
key_points: Start with simple products and build your skills gradually.
Keep your tools and workspace organized for efficiency.
Advertise your services in the community and through social media.
Maintain quality and deliver work on time to build a good reputation.
Keep track of your expenses and profits for sustainability.
lessons.local_example: A young tailor in Lilongwe sewing and selling made-to-order school uniforms.

quiz.question: What tool is used to measure the body accurately?

Which of these is NOT a basic sewing stitch?

options: Cut on a flat surface with good lighting
quiz.answer: Cut on a flat surface with good lighting

quiz.question: Which fabric is commonly used for everyday wear because it is breathable?
What is the purpose of hemming a garment?
options: To finish raw edges and prevent fraying
quiz.answer: To finish raw edges and prevent fraying

quiz.question: How often should you clean and oil your sewing machine?
What is a good first project for a beginner tailor?
Which alteration involves taking in or letting out seams?
Why is record keeping important in a tailoring business?

modules.title: Computer Skills
modules.description: Learn the essential computer skills needed for work, school, and daily tasks. This module covers how to use Microsoft Office tools (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), send emails, and store files using Google Drive.

lessons.title: Introduction to Computers and Typing
lessons.content: Before using Microsoft Office, it's important to know how to use a computer. Learn how to turn it on, use a keyboard and mouse, and open basic applications.
key_points: Use the power button to turn the computer on/off properly.
Practice typing with both hands using the keyboard.
Use a mouse to click, drag, and scroll.
Understand what a desktop, folder, and file are.
lessons.local_example: Helping a small shopkeeper type and print price lists using a desktop computer.

lessons.title: Using Microsoft Word
lessons.content: Microsoft Word is used for typing letters, creating documents, and making reports. It's one of the most common computer tools.
key_points: Open Word, type a letter, and save the file.
Use basic formatting tools: bold, underline, font size, and color.
Insert tables, pictures, and bullet points.
Save and print documents when ready.
lessons.local_example: Typing a business letter or a CV at a local internet café.

lessons.title: Using Microsoft Excel
lessons.content: Microsoft Excel is used to record and calculate data using tables. It helps manage money, stock, or lists.
key_points: Understand what a spreadsheet is (rows and columns).
Enter numbers and text into cells.
Use formulas like =SUM(A1:A5) to calculate totals.
Create simple charts to show information clearly.
lessons.local_example: Tracking a small business's sales using Excel tables and totals.

lessons.title: Using Microsoft PowerPoint
lessons.content: PowerPoint is used for creating presentations to teach or explain something with slides.
key_points: Create a new slide presentation.
Add text, images, and bullet points to slides.
Use slide transitions and animations.
Practice presenting using full-screen slideshow mode.
lessons.local_example: Preparing a farming tips presentation for a youth training event.

lessons.title: Creating and Sending Emails
lessons.content: Email is a way to send messages and documents using the internet. Gmail and Yahoo Mail are common services.
key_points: Create a free email account on Gmail or Yahoo.
Use To, CC, Subject, and Message fields correctly.
Attach documents or photos to an email.
Check your inbox and reply to messages.
lessons.local_example: Sending a job application with a CV and cover letter using email.

lessons.title: Using Google Drive for Cloud Storage
lessons.content: Google Drive allows you to save files online. This means your work is safe and accessible from any device.
key_points: Login with your Google account to access Google Drive.
Upload and download files from the cloud.
Organize files into folders.
Share documents with others using links or email.
lessons.local_example: Storing photos and important certificates in Google Drive for backup.

lessons.title: Safety and Good Habits in Computer Use
lessons.content: Using computers safely protects your work and your health. Good habits make you more productive.
key_points: Take breaks to avoid eye strain and back pain.
Save your work often to avoid losing data.
Avoid downloading files from unknown websites.
Use antivirus software and avoid spam emails.
lessons.local_example: Helping learners use a shared computer safely in a school lab.

quiz.question: Which tool is best for typing a letter?
What is Excel mainly used for?
Which app helps you create slides for a presentation?
Where can you store files online safely?
Which of these is a good computer safety habit?
options: Taking breaks and saving work often
quiz.answer: Taking breaks and saving work often

quiz.question: What do you need to send an email?

modules.title: Social Media Marketing
modules.description: Learn how to take better photos using a smartphone and use social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok to promote your business or personal brand.

lessons.title: Taking Good Photos with a Smartphone
lessons.content: You don’t need an expensive camera to take great photos. Most smartphones today can take clear and beautiful pictures if used correctly. Good photography helps you attract more people to your posts or products.
key_points: Clean your phone camera lens before taking photos.
Use natural lighting whenever possible — morning or late afternoon is best.
Keep your hands steady or use a stand to avoid blurry images.
Use the grid feature to align your photo and follow the ‘rule of thirds’.
Take multiple shots and choose the best one.
lessons.local_example: Taking clear, well-lit photos of mandasi or clothes to post on WhatsApp groups and Facebook Marketplace.

lessons.title: Editing and Enhancing Photos
lessons.content: Basic editing makes your photos look more attractive and professional. You can use simple apps to improve brightness, contrast, and sharpness.
key_points: Use free apps like Snapseed, Lightroom, or your phone’s photo editor.
Avoid over-editing — aim for natural colors.
Crop out distractions and focus on the product.
Add your name or logo if you are running a business.
lessons.local_example: Using Snapseed to brighten photos of handmade handbags before posting them online.

lessons.title: Basics of Social Media Marketing
lessons.content: Marketing on social media helps you reach more people and sell products easily. It's cheaper than traditional advertising and great for small businesses.
key_points: Use Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok to post your products or services.
Post regularly to stay visible to your followers.
Respond to comments and messages quickly to build trust.
Use hashtags (e.g., #mandasi #MadeInMalawi) to reach more people.
Join local buy-and-sell groups to post your products.
lessons.local_example: Posting photos of freshly baked cakes on Facebook every Friday to attract weekend customers.

lessons.title: Creating Content for Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok
lessons.content: Different social media platforms work in different ways. Knowing how to create the right content helps your business grow.
key_points: Use Facebook for posts, pictures, and longer descriptions.
Use Instagram for high-quality images and short videos with good captions.
Use TikTok for fun and short videos showing how your product is made or used.
Include prices, contact details, and location in your posts.
Use stories, reels, or status updates to show daily activity and new items.
lessons.local_example: Recording a short video while sewing a dress and posting it on TikTok with background music.

lessons.title: Tips for Growing Your Online Presence
lessons.content: Building a strong social media presence takes time and consistency. These tips help you grow your followers and turn them into customers.
key_points: Post high-quality photos consistently (e.g., 3–5 times per week).
Engage with your audience by replying and asking questions.
Follow and learn from others who sell similar items online.
Share your posts to WhatsApp groups and encourage sharing.
Ask happy customers to tag or mention your page.
lessons.local_example: Asking a friend to share your baking business post with her WhatsApp group for more exposure.

quiz.question: What is one way to take better photos with a smartphone?
options: Take photos in a dark room
Use natural light and hold the phone steady
quiz.answer: Use natural light and hold the phone steady

quiz.question: Why is editing photos important?
options: To make them look clearer and more attractive
quiz.answer: To make them look clearer and more attractive

quiz.question: What is a good reason to use hashtags?
What type of content is best for TikTok?
How can you grow your social media presence?
options: Post low-quality photos once a month
Post consistently and engage with followers
quiz.answer: Post consistently and engage with followers

modules.title: Basic Baking at Home
modules.description: Learn to bake mandasi, cakes, and bread using simple ingredients and basic techniques. This module will guide you through measuring, mixing, baking, and serving delicious homemade baked goods.

lessons.title: Ingredients and Tools
lessons.content: Baking starts with gathering the right ingredients and tools. Cleanliness is very important to make safe and tasty food. Make sure to measure your ingredients carefully for the best results.
key_points: Clean hands, bowls, utensils, and baking surfaces before starting.
Basic ingredients include flour, sugar, baking powder, yeast, eggs, salt, and oil or butter.
Common tools are mixing bowls, spoons, measuring cups, baking trays, frying pan, and oven or stove.
Use fresh ingredients for better taste and safety.
lessons.local_example: Using locally available maize flour and sugar to bake mandasi for market sale.

lessons.title: Making Mandasi (Fritters)
lessons.content: Mandasi is a popular fried dough snack. Mixing the right ingredients and allowing the dough to rise properly results in soft and tasty mandasi.
key_points: Mix flour, sugar, baking powder or yeast, water, and a little oil to form dough.
Let the dough rest and rise in a warm place for 30-60 minutes.
Heat oil properly and fry the mandasi until golden brown, turning to cook evenly.
Drain fried mandasi on paper towels to remove excess oil before serving.
lessons.local_example: Selling fresh mandasi at local church events and school functions.

lessons.title: Baking Simple Cakes
lessons.content: Learn the basics of baking a simple cake using flour, sugar, eggs, and baking powder. This lesson covers mixing, baking, and testing for doneness.
key_points: Preheat the oven or charcoal stove before starting to bake.
Cream sugar and eggs together before adding flour for a soft texture.
Use baking powder to help the cake rise.
Pour batter into a greased baking tin and bake for 30-45 minutes.
Test doneness by inserting a toothpick; it should come out clean.
lessons.local_example: Baking vanilla or banana cakes to sell at local markets and events.

lessons.title: Making Homemade Bread
lessons.content: Bread making involves mixing, kneading, rising, shaping, and baking dough. This lesson introduces these steps in simple terms.
key_points: Use flour, water, yeast, sugar, salt, and oil for bread dough.
Knead the dough well to develop gluten which makes bread soft.
Let the dough rise twice: first after mixing and then after shaping.
Bake at a moderate temperature until the crust is golden brown.
Cool bread on a wire rack before slicing.
lessons.local_example: Making fresh bread for breakfast or sale in the neighborhood.

lessons.title: Baking Safety and Hygiene
lessons.content: Keeping your baking area clean and following safety rules prevents accidents and food contamination.
key_points: Wash hands before handling food.
Keep work surfaces and tools clean.
Be careful when handling hot ovens, pans, and oil.
Store ingredients properly to avoid spoilage.
Dispose of waste safely.
lessons.local_example: Teaching young bakers in a community group about cleanliness and safety.

lessons.title: Tips for Better Baking Results
lessons.content: Small changes in your technique and ingredients can improve your baking outcome.
key_points: Always measure ingredients accurately.
Use fresh yeast and baking powder for good rising.
Don’t overmix batter to avoid tough cakes.
Let baked goods cool before serving.
Experiment with flavors like vanilla, cinnamon, or local fruits.
lessons.local_example: Adding mashed bananas to cake batter to create a popular local flavor.

quiz.question: Which ingredient helps dough rise?
What should you do before baking?
Why is it important to let mandasi dough rise?
options: To make it easier to mix
To make mandasi soft and fluffy
quiz.answer: To make mandasi soft and fluffy

quiz.question: How do you check if a cake is done baking?
options: Insert a toothpick to see if it comes out clean
quiz.answer: Insert a toothpick to see if it comes out clean

quiz.question: What is the purpose of kneading bread dough?
options: To develop gluten for soft bread
quiz.answer: To develop gluten for soft bread

quiz.question: What safety rule should you follow when baking?

modules.title: Mobile Money Payments
modules.description: Learn how to register, use, and manage mobile money services like Airtel Money and TNM Mpamba for safe and simple financial transactions. This module also teaches how to avoid scams and use mobile money for daily needs like buying airtime or paying bills.

lessons.title: Introduction to Mobile Money
lessons.content: Mobile money allows you to send, receive, and store money using your phone. You do not need a bank account to use it, and it works in both rural and urban areas.
key_points: Popular services in Malawi include Airtel Money and TNM Mpamba.
You only need a SIM card, a phone, and a national ID to register.
You can send money to others, pay bills, and buy airtime anytime.
Mobile money saves time and reduces the need to carry cash.
lessons.local_example: Registering for Airtel Money at a shop to receive money from relatives in town.

lessons.title: How to Register and Use Mobile Money
lessons.content: Getting started is easy. Once you register, you will be able to perform many financial tasks using USSD codes or mobile apps.
key_points: Register with your ID card and phone at an agent shop or mobile kiosk.
Set a secret PIN and never share it with anyone.
Use shortcodes like *211# for Airtel or *444# for TNM to access services.
Follow the menu to send money, buy airtime, or pay bills.
lessons.local_example: Using *211# to send school fees to a family member using Airtel Money.

lessons.title: Sending, Receiving, and Withdrawing Money
lessons.content: Mobile money lets you transfer funds securely from one person to another or withdraw as physical cash when needed.
key_points: Always double-check the receiver's phone number before sending.
You will receive an SMS after a successful transaction.
To withdraw cash, go to a nearby agent with your ID and phone.
Agents charge small fees for transactions — always ask for a receipt.
lessons.local_example: Receiving money from a customer after selling a dress and withdrawing it at the nearest Mpamba agent.

lessons.title: Avoiding Mobile Money Scams
lessons.content: Scammers use tricks to steal money. Stay alert and never trust strangers who ask for money or your PIN.
key_points: Never share your PIN, even with family or agents.
Ignore messages saying you won a prize or promotion.
Do not follow strange links or call back unknown numbers.
Report suspicious messages or calls to customer service.
lessons.local_example: Ignoring a fake SMS that said, 'You have won K100,000. Send PIN to claim.'

lessons.title: Using Mobile Money to Buy Airtime and Pay Bills
lessons.content: Mobile money can help you pay for services without needing to go to town or queue. It saves time and transport costs.
key_points: Buy airtime for yourself or others using the mobile money menu.
Pay electricity (ESCOM), TV subscriptions (like GOtv), or water bills easily.
Some payments can be done directly through mobile apps.
Keep SMS confirmations as proof of payment.
lessons.local_example: Paying for electricity units (token) using TNM Mpamba without leaving the house.

quiz.question: What do you need to register for mobile money?
options: Phone, SIM card, and national ID
quiz.answer: Phone, SIM card, and national ID

quiz.question: Which one is a correct shortcode for Airtel Money?
Why should you never share your mobile money PIN?
options: Because it is hard to remember
So others can use your money
To protect your account from theft
It’s okay to share with friends
quiz.answer: To protect your account from theft

quiz.question: What should you do if someone asks for your PIN by SMS?
What can you pay for using mobile money?

modules.title: Design & Fashion
modules.description: Learn the basics of fashion design, fabric selection, and how to sew clothing for special occasions. This module helps you grow your tailoring skills into a creative and profitable business.

lessons.title: Basic Fashion Design and Sketching
lessons.content: Fashion design begins with creative ideas that are drawn on paper. Sketching helps you visualize clothing before cutting the fabric. It is an important step for custom tailoring.
key_points: Start with simple body outlines and draw the clothing style over it.
Use pencils, colored pens, or simple apps for sketching ideas.
Add notes like sleeve type, neck design, or fabric choice to your sketch.
Keep a sketchbook to record ideas and customer requests.
Practice drawing common styles like skirts, blouses, trousers, and dresses.
lessons.local_example: Sketching a chitenje dress design for a customer going to a wedding.

lessons.title: Choosing Fabrics and Colors
lessons.content: Fabric choice affects comfort, look, and the success of your design. Understanding colors and textures helps you give better fashion advice to customers.
key_points: Use cotton or polyester for daily wear; satin, lace, and silk for special events.
Bold colors work well for festivals; soft colors for formal wear.
Match fabrics to the weather — lighter for hot seasons, heavier for cold.
Mix textures like lace with cotton for stylish effects.
Help customers choose colors based on their skin tone and event type.
lessons.local_example: Using white satin with blue lace for a bridal outfit requested by a client.

lessons.title: Sewing Styles for Special Occasions
lessons.content: Special occasions require unique styles with more detail. As a tailor, you must sew with care and use quality finishes for weddings, parties, and church wear.
key_points: Popular styles include flare dresses, pencil skirts, suits, and shirts with embroidery.
Use zippers, buttons, beads, and lace to add beauty.
Always fit the garment on the client before finishing.
Pay attention to symmetry, curves, and clean stitching.
Iron the garment and package it neatly before delivery.
lessons.local_example: Sewing matching family outfits (his & hers) for a church celebration.

quiz.question: Why is sketching important in fashion design?
Which fabric is best for a wedding dress?
What should you do before completing a dress for an event?
Which colors are best for formal wear?
What makes a dress suitable for a special event?
options: Using beads, lace, and a good fit
quiz.answer: Using beads, lace, and a good fit

modules.title: Basic Entrepreneurship
modules.description: Learn how to start and manage a small business, budget your money, attract and keep customers, and keep simple financial records to grow a successful business.

lessons.title: Starting a Small Business
lessons.content: Starting a business begins with identifying a problem or need and finding a simple solution. You don’t need big capital — just a good idea and a plan.
key_points: Think of a product or service people in your area need.
Start small with what you have and grow over time.
Write down your business idea, plan your steps, and set goals.
Talk to others who are running small businesses and learn from them.
Choose a good location or platform (e.g., roadside stall, home, or online).
lessons.local_example: Starting a mandasi business near a school with just flour, oil, and a frying pan.

lessons.title: Budgeting and Saving
lessons.content: Budgeting helps you plan your income and expenses so that you don’t overspend. Saving helps you grow your business or handle emergencies.
key_points: Record all income and spending each week.
Separate business money from personal money.
Buy what you need, not just what you want.
Save a little from each sale or profit.
Use savings to grow your business, not for luxury.
lessons.local_example: Saving part of daily profits from tailoring to buy a better sewing machine.

lessons.title: Customer Service Skills
lessons.content: Happy customers will return and tell others about your business. Customer service means treating customers with respect and honesty.
key_points: Greet customers politely and listen to their needs.
Keep promises — deliver on time and provide good quality.
Accept feedback and improve where necessary.
Handle complaints calmly and find solutions.
Say 'thank you' and follow up if possible (e.g., via WhatsApp).
lessons.local_example: A young entrepreneur making custom aprons and sending photos to customers before delivery to confirm design.

lessons.title: Marketing Basics (Online and Offline)
lessons.content: Marketing is how you tell people about your product. Use simple tools to promote your business — both online and in your community.
key_points: Use flyers, word of mouth, posters, and signs for offline marketing.
Take good photos and post them on WhatsApp, Facebook, or TikTok.
Join buy-and-sell groups or pages to reach more people.
Offer promotions or discounts to attract new customers.
Use branding — like wearing a branded apron or using labels.
lessons.local_example: Posting freshly baked cakes on Facebook with prices and contact info.

lessons.title: Record Keeping and Bookkeeping
lessons.content: Keeping records helps you know if your business is making profit or loss. It also helps you plan better and stay organized.
key_points: Write down every sale, cost, and profit in a simple notebook.
Use a cashbook or daily expense tracker.
Keep receipts and supplier contact info safely.
Review your records weekly or monthly.
Know your profit margin: Total Sales – Total Costs = Profit.
lessons.local_example: A market vendor tracking tomato sales and costs daily to calculate weekly profits.

modules.title: Basic Farming Skills
modules.description: Learn how to grow crops effectively, prepare land, manage pests, and improve your harvest with simple, practical farming techniques.

lessons.title: Soil Preparation
lessons.content: Good farming starts with proper soil preparation. Preparing the soil well improves water retention, aeration, and nutrient availability for crops.
key_points: Remove weeds and old plant debris before planting.
Tilling or turning the soil helps loosen it for root growth.
Add organic manure or compost to enrich the soil naturally.
Test soil texture; sandy soils drain fast, clay soils hold water longer.
Make ridges or beds based on the type of crop and land slope.
lessons.local_example: Using compost made from maize husks, cow dung, and kitchen waste to enrich soil in a village garden.

lessons.title: Planting and Spacing
lessons.content: Planting seeds or seedlings at the correct depth and spacing is crucial for healthy crop development and good yield.
key_points: Follow recommended spacing: for example, maize should be spaced about 75cm apart.
Plant seeds at the right depth, usually between 2 to 5cm depending on the crop.
Use clean, treated seeds to reduce disease risk and improve germination.
Water seeds gently after planting to avoid washing them away.
Thin out crowded seedlings to prevent competition for nutrients.
lessons.local_example: Spacing tomato seedlings properly in backyard gardens in Lilongwe to improve air circulation and fruit size.

lessons.title: Watering and Irrigation
lessons.content: Providing enough water is essential for crop growth, especially during dry periods.
key_points: Water crops early in the morning or late in the afternoon to reduce evaporation.
Avoid overwatering which can cause root rot or fungal diseases.
Use simple irrigation methods such as drip or basin irrigation where possible.
Mulch around plants to conserve soil moisture and reduce weeds.
lessons.local_example: Using rainwater harvesting barrels to irrigate small gardens during dry spells.

lessons.title: Pest and Disease Management
lessons.content: Protecting crops from pests and diseases is vital for a good harvest.
key_points: Regularly inspect crops for signs of pests or disease.
Use natural pest control methods like companion planting and organic pesticides.
Remove infected plants quickly to prevent spread.
Rotate crops each season to reduce pest build-up.
Practice good farm hygiene by cleaning tools and equipment.
lessons.local_example: Using neem leaves as a natural pesticide to control aphids on cabbage crops.

lessons.title: Harvesting and Storage
lessons.content: Harvest crops at the right time and store them properly to maintain quality and reduce losses.
key_points: Harvest maize when kernels are hard and dry.
Pick fruits and vegetables early in the morning when cool.
Dry crops like maize and beans thoroughly before storage.
Store crops in a cool, dry place protected from pests and moisture.
Use traditional storage methods like granaries or improved bags.
lessons.local_example: Drying maize cobs in the sun and storing them in traditional granaries to prevent mold.
